title: Query-driven workload oracle and bench suite for kernel/attention scheduling
creator: Aisha Kumar
description:
Goal: Deliver a query-driven workload oracle and a companion benchmark suite that exercises kernel selection, attention-mode variants, and prefill/decode scheduling strategies across representative production distributions. This ticket consolidates a reproducible generator for small/mid/long sequence queries, a golden-run validator that computes statistical deltas against golden baselines, and CI perf gates that fail on regressions in p50/p95/p99 for both latency and token-throughput.

Scope and deliverables:
- Workload oracle: a query-config DSL (JSON lines) which encodes sequence-length histograms, prompt complexity tags, attention-mode hints (e.g., flash/causal/fused), KV cache reuse ratios, and expected decode branching. The oracle will be used to synthesize deterministic request traces for replay and stochastic mutation.
- Query-driven generator: a small binary (benchgen) that consumes the oracle DSL and emits replay traces + lightweight telemetry hooks compatible with our existing trace-replay harness. Supports seeding for deterministic fuzzing.
- Golden baseline matrix: curated baseline metrics per model family (e.g., redwood-3B, LL-Fast-7B, open-suite-13B) across prefills (short/medium/long) and decode profiles. Baselines stored as compressed CSVs and a JSON manifest with per-bucket thresholds.
- CI perf gates: new pipeline stage (bench-compare) that runs the generator against PR clusters for a 10-minute representative run, computes quantiles and perf-regression deltas, and raises warnings/fails if regressions exceed configurable thresholds.
- Observability integrations: telemetry keys for kernel selection counts, attention-mode switch rates, prefill-slice latency, decode-batch utilization, and KV-cache hit ratios. Ensure these emit to existing console dashboards.

Design decisions and trade-offs:
- Deterministic vs stochastic workloads: primary CI runs will use deterministic seeds to ensure repeatability; nightly fuzz runs will use stochastic variants to catch non-deterministic interactions (e.g., scheduling/race conditions).
- Synthetic vs production trace fidelity: we will implement a hybrid approach where synthetic queries are shaped by sampled production histograms (privacy-preserving, aggregated). This balances coverage and privacy.
- Failure sensitivity: CI gates use both relative deltas and absolute thresholds. Small regressions (<=3% p95 latency) produce warnings; larger regressions (>7% or >20ms absolute) fail the gate.

Implementation plan:
1) Define oracle DSL and manifest format; PR with schema and examples (benchgen input).
2) Implement benchgen in Rust (shared with existing harness) with options for replay and streaming mode.
3) Add kernel-selection hooks in runtime to tag decisions (minimal perf overhead tracing mode).
4) Create golden baseline ingestion tool and manifest store under s3://redwood-golden/benchmarks/runtime-1.21/.
5) Wire bench-compare job into CI; add gating thresholds to repo config.
6) Dashboard panels and alert rules for regressions; link to PR diff output.

Risks and mitigations:
- Extra CI time: mitigate by limiting CI runs to short deterministic seeds and offloading heavy fuzzing to nightly.
- False positives from noisy quantiles: use bootstrapped confidence intervals and require regressions across two consecutive runs before automatic rollbacks.
- Instrumentation overhead: add low-overhead kernel tagging flag and ensure it's disabled in production warm paths.

Acceptance criteria:
- benchgen binary that can produce a 10-minute representative trace in <3 minutes wall time on CI test cluster.
- Golden baseline manifest published for at least 3 model families and 3 sequence buckets.
- CI bench-compare stage executed on PRs and failing when configured thresholds are exceeded.
- Dashboard panels display kernel-selection distribution and prefill latency by model/sequence bucket.
